title: StubHub International tells customers contact data may have been exposed
summary: StubHub International, run by Ticketbis S.L., began emailing customers on 10 November, per TickSights as relayed by TicketNews, after detecting unauthorised access to certain systems between late October and early November. Names, email addresses, phone numbers and country settings may have been exposed. A spokesperson confirmed the access and said authorities were notified, with no evidence of access to passwords or payment details. No customer count has been given.
plain: A ticket resale site warned customers that their names, emails and phone numbers may have leaked. It says it found no evidence that payment details were accessed.
exec: Exposed contact details enable convincing phishing against ticket buyers.
action: General advice: StubHub International customers should treat unexpected messages claiming to be StubHub with suspicion and not click their links.
date_note: TicketNews, citing a TickSights report of 11 November, says StubHub International began sending customer notifications the previous day (10 November); the access itself happened between late October and early November per the notices. The Register reported on 18 November.

validation.note: The Register read; TicketNews read and adds a StubHub International spokesperson statement, citing TickSights for the 10 November notification date; both describe the same customer notices, so one original report. LavX repeats it.

review.note: stronger than the source: plain said no payment details were taken, sources say no evidence found; validation note corrected (TicketNews cites TickSights)
